summary.text: Son of Talaemenes and captain of the Maeonians whose birth was beneath Tmolas — brother of Antiphus, whose mother was the nymph of the Gygaean lake.

story.text: Nestor's muster-roll names Mesthles and Antiphus, the two sons of Talaemenes, as captains twain of the Maeonians. Apollodorus repeats the parentage in the catalogue of Trojan allies.
When the fight turned about Patroclus' body, Hector went to and fro heartening the allied tribes and named Mesthles among the captains he roused to stand against the Danaans.
